name: Tongue cleaners/scrapers
anchor: sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant schedules with the Germany BVL 2017 TOOTHPASTE tier as the oral-mucosal anchor for formulated products, and Canada SOR/2018-83's mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling as the article anchor
native_basis: oral-care article as placed on market (total content per accessible part, ug/kg)
native_basis_label: oral-care article as placed on market — total heavy-metal content of each accessible part, per unit mass of that component's material (ug/kg). Not a cosmetic finished-product basis, not a dietary maximum level, and not an EN 71-3 migration/leachate value.
scope_note: Tongue scrapers and cleaners in stainless steel, copper and copper-alloy, and polymer, and the tongue-cleaning face moulded onto some toothbrush heads (which is certified with the brush on the toothbrushes row). These are ARTICLES and no cosmetic finished-product contaminant limit reaches them. Copper-alloy scrapers are the highest-risk form in the row: leaded brasses and bronzes are common in low-cost cast and machined copper articles, and REACH's brass derogation at 0.5% lead by weight is explicitly NOT used here — the Canadian 90 mg/kg accessible-part ceiling is applied to copper-alloy scrapers without derogation, because the derogation is a machinability allowance rather than a health finding.
basis_guard: ^(?!.*(cosmetic|migration|leachate|colourant|colorant|surface coating|sticker|as consumed|wet weight|candy))(?=.*(content in accessible part|concentration by weight in article))
basis_guard_note: An oral-care article is not a cosmetic and is not a food. The guard admits only article material-content instruments (Canada SOR/2018-83 accessible-part lead content; REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) lead concentration by weight in a mouthable article) and rejects (a) finished-cosmetic impurity limits, which are written for a formulated product and cannot be applied to a polymer filament or a stainless-steel staple, (b) EN 71-3 / Directive 2009/48 toy values, which are MIGRATION limits and would understate content by orders of magnitude if read as content, and (c) surface-coating and sticker instruments, which govern an applied film rather than the substrate.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit default), Category 20 Oral Care: a formulated oral product takes the strictest applicable sovereign finished-cosmetic contaminant maximum in its as-sold basis, with the Germany BVL 2017 toothpaste tier read across to non-toothpaste oral-mucosal forms where it is stricter; an oral-care article takes the Canadian mouth-contact accessible-part lead ceiling and is otherwise held under component-level control. Species never replace totals, no ingredient purity specification anchors a finished-product cell, no migration value anchors a content cell, and no cell is occurrence-derived.

Pb.basis: total lead content per accessible part, ug/kg of that component's material (article content basis, not migration)
Pb.label: Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83) reach mouth-contact consumer products, and section 2(1) caps EACH ACCESSIBLE PART of such a product at 90 mg/kg total lead. An oral-care article is a consumer product brought into contact with the user's mouth in the course of normal use, so the Canadian value directly regulates this cell on the article's own content basis. The only other article-scoped sovereign lead CONTENT instrument in the register, REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) as added by Regulation (EU) 2015/628, sets 0.05% lead by weight (500 mg/kg) for articles that may be placed in the mouth by children; it is five and a half times looser and does not bind.
Pb.substantiation: The Canadian ceiling is applied to every accessible part of the finished article, not to a composite of the whole product, because that is how section 2(1) is written; a composite-averaged result would dilute a leaded component against inert bulk and is not accepted. Components tested separately: the scraping edge and blade (stainless steel, copper alloy or polymer), the handle or loop, any plating or surface treatment, and any elastomeric grip. The scraping edge is sampled separately from the handle because it is the part in abrasive mucosal contact and, on plated articles, carries the plating chemistry. Two allowances written into the cited instruments are deliberately NOT taken: SOR/2018-83 section 2(2)'s conditional essential-characteristic exception, which substitutes a release criterion for the content criterion, and the REACH entry 63(8)(g) brass-alloy derogation at 0.5% lead by weight. Both are machinability and functional-necessity allowances rather than health findings, and HMTc certifies against the content criterion without them. The EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are likewise not used: they are migration limits on a leachate basis, and reading a migration number as a content ceiling is the basis conflation this row's guard exists to prevent.

Cd.rationale: No sovereign sets a cadmium content limit for a mouth-contact oral-care article. Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83), the only instrument scoped to mouth-contact consumer products on a total-content basis, is lead-only — as is the second article-content lead instrument named in this row's own lead cell, REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) as added by Regulation (EU) 2015/628; the EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are MIGRATION limits and are excluded by this row's basis guard, and finished-cosmetic impurity schedules are written for a formulated product and do not reach an article. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: cadmium is a known pigment and polymer-stabiliser residue in coloured plastics and a plating-bath contaminant, both of which are present in this article class. Two total-content cadmium restrictions in the register reach articles supplied to the general public without being scoped to oral care, and both are recorded and disposed of rather than adopted. REACH Annex XVII entry 23 paragraph 1 (eu_494_2011_cd_plastic_materials_0_01pct, 100000 ug/kg = 0.01 percent by weight) restricts cadmium in mixtures and articles produced from a listed set of synthetic organic polymers, so a polymer handle, floss-pick body or irrigator tip may fall inside it depending on which polymers the entry lists. Minnesota Statutes section 325E.3892 (mn_325e3892_2025_cd_covered_consumer_products_75ppm, 75000 ug/kg by total product or component weight) restricts cadmium in a listed set of covered consumer products. Neither is scoped to a mouth-contact oral-care article; both are excluded mechanically by this row's basis guard, because their register bases are a polymer-material basis and a whole-product weight basis rather than the accessible-part content basis this row publishes on; and each is a permissive numeric threshold, whereas this cell publishes no ceiling and dispositions results under ALARA with supplier corrective action. Adopting either as a ceiling would relax the cell rather than tighten it, which Method v2.0 does not permit.
Cd.reference_method: Mandatory per-lot total-content analysis by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold, with COMPONENT-LEVEL sampling of the finished article (the scraping edge and blade (stainless steel, copper alloy or polymer), the handle or loop, any plating or surface treatment, and any elastomeric grip) — each component digested and reported separately, with no composite-averaged result accepted. No numeric ceiling is published; results are dispositioned under the HMTc control-and-escalation rule (ALARA against the tightest available context plus supplier corrective action on the identified component).

iAs.rationale: Inorganic arsenic is the toxic fraction of total arsenic and no jurisdiction sets an inorganic-arsenic content limit for a consumer article; every sovereign inorganic-arsenic maximum level in the register is a food, feed or fertiliser commodity value on a dietary or dry-matter basis (rice and rice products, fish and other marine products, fruit juice, milk and dairy, meat and offal, sugar, edible salt, edible oils and fats, gelatine and collagen, pet food, and the EU fertilising-product classes), and not one is scoped to a cosmetic, an oral-care product or a consumer article. The cell is governed by reflex speciation off the total-arsenic control rather than by an invented ceiling.
iAs.reference_method: Reflex HPLC-ICP-MS inorganic-arsenic speciation on any component (the scraping edge and blade (stainless steel, copper alloy or polymer), the handle or loop, any plating or surface treatment, and any elastomeric grip) whose total-arsenic screen is confirmed above the analytical reporting limit. The inorganic fraction is held under ALARA and triggers supplier corrective action on the identified component.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a polymer filament, elastomer, wood stick or stainless-steel component, and no jurisdiction sets a methylmercury limit for a consumer article. It is held as a control rather than registered as a speciation-bounded not-material determination because this row's total-mercury parent is itself a control with no published ceiling: a speciation-bounded claim requires a published total-element parent to bound the species against, and this row has none. Mercury is therefore governed through the total-mercury control.
MeHg.reference_method: Total-mercury screen by microwave-assisted closed-vessel acid digestion (HNO3/H2O2) with ICP-MS determination, reported as ug/kg of product as sold on each component (the scraping edge and blade (stainless steel, copper alloy or polymer), the handle or loop, any plating or surface treatment, and any elastomeric grip). Methylmercury speciation (GC-ICP-MS, EPA 1630) is required only where a confirmed total-mercury result cannot be traced to an inorganic input.

Sn.rationale: No sovereign sets a tin content limit for a mouth-contact oral-care article. Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83), the only instrument scoped to mouth-contact consumer products on a total-content basis, is lead-only — as is the second article-content lead instrument named in this row's own lead cell, REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) as added by Regulation (EU) 2015/628; the EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are MIGRATION limits and are excluded by this row's basis guard, and finished-cosmetic impurity schedules are written for a formulated product and do not reach an article. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: organotin and tin-catalyst residues occur in silicone and polyurethane elastomers and tin occurs in solders and plating, all of which appear in this article class. The register's tin restrictions that reach articles supplied to the general public are SPECIATED organotin restrictions and are a different measurand from this total-tin cell. REACH Annex XVII entry 20 paragraph 3 (eu_reach_entry20_dbt_general_public_articles_0_1pct) caps dibutyltin compounds expressed as tin at 0.1 percent by weight in mixtures and articles supplied to the general public, and the companion paragraph (eu_reach_entry20_dot_skin_contact_articles_0_1pct) caps dioctyltin the same way in skin-contact and childcare articles. Both restrict the use of a named organotin class rather than setting a total-tin content maximum, both are excluded mechanically by this row's basis guard, and at 1000000 ug/kg as tin both are permissive thresholds against a cell that publishes no ceiling and dispositions under ALARA. They are recorded and not adopted.

Cr.rationale: No sovereign sets a total chromium content limit for a mouth-contact oral-care article. Canada's Consumer Products Containing Lead Regulations (SOR/2018-83), the only instrument scoped to mouth-contact consumer products on a total-content basis, is lead-only — as is the second article-content lead instrument named in this row's own lead cell, REACH Annex XVII entry 63(7) as added by Regulation (EU) 2015/628; the EU toy values (Directive 2009/48 / EN 71-3) are MIGRATION limits and are excluded by this row's basis guard, and finished-cosmetic impurity schedules are written for a formulated product and do not reach an article. The cell is held under mandatory analytical control, not declared not-material: chromium is a defining alloying element of the stainless steel used for staples, wires and tips and is present in chrome plating and in Cr(III) pigments; total chromium is a screen for the Cr(VI) reflex below and is not itself protective.

Cr-VI.rationale: No jurisdiction sets a hexavalent-chromium content limit scoped to an oral-care article. Four Cr(VI) CONTENT restrictions in the register do reach consumer articles of other kinds, and each is recorded and disposed of rather than adopted: China GB 28480-2012 (cn_gb28480_2012_cr_vi_adornment_total_1000) caps 1000000 ug/kg total content in metal adornment materials and components; REACH Annex XVII entry 47 as added by Regulation (EU) 301/2014 (eu_301_2014_cr_vi_leather_articles_3mgkg) caps 3000 ug/kg on the dry weight of leather in skin-contact leather articles; Regulation (EU) 2018/1513 (eu_2018_1513_cr_vi_consumer_textiles_1mgkg) caps 1000 ug/kg in skin-contact consumer textiles after extraction; and the RoHS Directive (eu_rohs_2011_crvi_homogeneous_materials_1000000) caps 0.1 percent by weight in the homogeneous materials of electrical and electronic equipment, which does reach the motor, shaft, drive and plated components of a powered brush head or oral irrigator. None is scoped to a mouth-contact oral-care article, none shares this row's accessible-part content basis (their bases are metal-adornment content, leather dry weight, textile extract and homogeneous-material weight respectively), and every one is a permissive threshold, whereas the disposition applied below fails the lot on any quantifiable Cr(VI) — so adopting any of them as a ceiling would relax the cell rather than tighten it. The EU toy figure (Directive 2009/48 Category II, 5 ug/kg) is separately excluded as a migration value on a leachate basis, which cannot be read as a content ceiling without the conflation this row's basis guard forbids. Cr(VI) is not registered as a method artifact here: chrome-plated and chromate-passivated metal parts, stainless-steel filament staples and orthodontic-grade wire are real Cr(VI) sources in mouth-contact articles, so an absence claim would not survive the substantiation gate. The cell is a control with reflex speciation and a zero-tolerance disposition.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Reflex Cr(VI) speciation (EPA 3060A alkaline extraction with IC-ICP-MS per EPA 6800, or EN 15192) on any component (the scraping edge and blade (stainless steel, copper alloy or polymer), the handle or loop, any plating or surface treatment, and any elastomeric grip) returning an elevated total-chromium screen. Any quantifiable Cr(VI) fails the lot and blocks release pending supplier corrective action.
